newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Eldorado says Gencor deal off.
newsitem.headline: Eldorado says Gencor deal off.

text.p: Canada's Eldorado Gold Corp Ltd said on Tuesday that a proposed $193.6 million deal with South Africa's Gencor Ltd had been called off due to market conditions.

"...Due to current market conditions, Eldorado and Gencor Ltd have been unable to satisfactorily renegotiate the proposed transaction previously announced on June 5, 1997," Eldorado said in a statement.
"As a result, the proposed transaction will not proceed," it added.

Gencor announced June 5 that it had signed a memorandum of understanding with Eldorado Gold Corp, in terms of which Eldorado would acquire a portfolio of mining and development and exploration assets in Ghana and South Africa in a deal valued at $193.6 million.
An Eldorado spokesman told Reuters current market conditions referred mainly to the recent weakness in the gold price.
Gold fell to a 12-year low of $314 an ounce in early July and has made little progress beyond $330 since then. It was trading at around $323 an ounce in late London trade on Tuesday.
Gencor declined to comment on the announcement and said a statement would be released on Wednesday.
Eldorado said it would continue to develop its ongoing relationship with the new Gencor Ltd.
Gencor recently split itself into base metals arm Billiton plc and a gold company Gencor Ltd -- Eldorado's largest shareholder.
"Eldorado intends to concentrate its activities on its present operations, development projects and priority exploration properties," the company added.
